heroOverlay.note: LandingHero.styles.ts previously recorded the source's rgba(0,0,0,0.45) overlay as dead markup that 'never paints', on the basis that reproducing it gives rgb(21,51,124), 'far too dark'. heroContentColumn.note: The hero does NOT use the site Wrapper (1170). It uses react-flexbox-grid's container, whose breakpoints are Bootstrap's 576/768/992/1200 with FIXED widths 560/752/976/1184 and 8px padding — a third breakpoint system alongside the site SCSS (360/470/768/1023/1200/1590) and Tailwind's.
heroContentColumn.accepted: The port's inner column is 1168 (matching the source's Col content exactly, so the bank strip is pixel-identical), but the 7/12 headline column measures 665 vs the source's 675 — a 10px difference from taking the fraction of 1168 rather than 1184. Accepted.

decisions.packageGridLiveChat: The source renders "live chat" inside the contact note as a <button> whose onclick opens a live-chat widget. This repo has NO chat provider (no Intercom/Crisp/Tawk/Zendesk/Drift anywhere in src/), so there is nothing to wire it to. Ported as colour-only emphasis: the CMS value carries {live chat}, which Text turns into an <em>, styled cyan/non-italic to match the source computed values exactly (rgb(0,177,227), normal, 400, no underline, cursor:auto). Deliberately NOT a button — a control that looks clickable and does nothing is worse than plain text. OPEN: pick a chat provider, then make this a real control.
decisions.packageGridTooltips: The source has 22 icon-only tooltip triggers on the highlight rows (interactive). This port renders the same info discs as plain <svg> with a title attribute — a static substitute, so check-completeness reports "22 unlabelled controls fewer in the port". Accepted for now; revisit with the chat/tooltip behaviour pass.
decisions.fourStepsMobileCard: SUPERSEDED by carouselImplementation — both sides now render a carousel at 390. The card box measures 328.02 here against the source's 311.98, but that is purely which box owns the description's 16px bottom margin: this port's slide is a flex item, which is a BFC root, so the margin cannot escape it, while the source's step is a plain block inside a Slide and the margin lands on the tray instead. Rendered result is identical — description-bottom to dots-top is 26px and first-dot-top is 36px on BOTH sides at 390 and 500. Do NOT "fix" this by scoping the margin to md: that removes the space entirely and cuts the real gap from 26 to 10.
decisions.carouselImplementation: The source renders TWO subtrees per carousel block (a desktop grid and a mobile carousel) and hides one with CSS. This port renders ONE list that is a snap scroller at small widths and a grid above, so there is no duplicated markup, no duplicated images and no duplicated headings for a screen reader. Dots come from src/components/shared/SnapCarousel and derive their count from scroll geometry (scrollWidth / clientWidth) rather than a slides-per-view constant, which is what lets each block set slides-per-view purely in Tailwind. Two deliberate improvements on the source: the active dot uses aria-current instead of the source's disabled attribute (which removes it from the tab order), and the track is focusable so keyboard users can scroll a carousel whose slides contain nothing focusable.
decisions.pageCanvas: The .theme-rapidformations canvas was rgb(4 4 41) (dark navy), inherited from the public-brand codebase this repo was seeded from. The Gatsby source paints its page canvas #ffffff, so every inter-block margin rendered as a navy band the source does not have. Changed --surface-canvas to rgb(255 255 255) on 2026-08-03. Safe: /home is the only page in the CMS, and all 87 visible text nodes that inherit the body colour sit on a background their own component paints (navy header, dropdown panels, blue hero, green buttons, brand bank tiles) — none relies on a dark canvas. Found by scripts/compare-page.mjs, not by any block-scoped check.
decisions.sectionWrapperNaming: SectionWrapper background options are misnamed for this brand now the canvas is light: "light" maps to --surface-primary (rgb 42 42 67, dark) and "dark" maps to --surface-canvas (now white). bCorpCertification asked for "light" and rendered navy; its CMS value was changed to "inverse". Left as-is rather than churning the mapping — re-derive both when the rest of the light theme is authored. Nothing else on /home uses either value.
decisions.richTextZebra: The .payload-richtext odd-row fill read var(--surface-canvas), which the canvas flip would have turned white-on-white. Repointed at var(--surface-on-light-sunken, var(--surface-canvas)) — the fallback keeps the QCF theme byte-identical, since that token is only defined for rapidformations.
decisions.fourStepsToBcorpGap: From 1023 up the source puts 160px between the fourSteps section and the B-Corp banner while fourSteps declares margin-bottom 140px at every width. The extra 20px is padding-bottom on the source wrapper Wrapper--wrapper__content--8eCpc, which groups the UNPORTED "Key questions about forming a company" FAQ section (source section 5) together with fourSteps. Deliberately NOT reproduced as a fabricated margin: once section 5 is ported the two are no longer adjacent and the wrapper is what carries the 20px. Re-check this gap when section 5 lands. Matches exactly at 390 and 768.
decisions.heroOverlayMobileOnly: The hero overlay is not dead markup. The source darkens the whole hero below 768 and sets the overlay to opacity 0 from 768 up, so sampling only at desktop shows raw brand blue. The painted mobile colour is rgb(21 51 124).
decisions.headerHeightBreakpoint: The header is 90px and becomes two rows at 1200; the hero switches its offset at 1023. --header-height therefore steps at 1023, the HERO breakpoint, because the hero is what consumes it. Between 1023 and 1199 the source pulls the hero up 151px against a 90px header and clips 61px of its own background — reproduced rather than tidied.
decisions.packageBandGrey: rgb(245 245 245) for the package grid band and rgb(240 240 240) for the footer are two tokens on purpose. 245 is exactly what the package band measures; the footer and five other places measure 240. Collapsing them would erase a real step between the package band and the footer directly beneath it.
decisions.fontSmoothing: The ported sections set -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased to match the source. No computed property reports it — both sides say font-weight 400 — so it only shows in a pixel diff. Scoped to the port utility so it changes the ported sections and nothing else.
decisions.headerNonHomeVariant: Ported 2026-08-03 from the source COMPONENT and STYLESHEET, not from a rendered page: the local Gatsby build only serves the home route and every other path returns 200 with an empty body, so there was nothing to measure. src/components/directus/navigation/Navigation.tsx toggles eleven things on an isHome prop; the ones that matter are navColor #ffffff (the bar is white on inner pages), navtab/navlist colour -font #595959 with hover -brand-blue-highlight #00b1e3, burgerColor #000000, the mobile menu wrapper -white instead of -black, and a different logo asset. Wired to the repo EXISTING isHeaderOnDark page field rather than a usePathname() check — the variant depends on whether the page opens with a dark hero, not on the URL. Carried to descendants by a data-on-light attribute on the header root, reusing the group-data-[scrolled] pattern already in the file, so no prop threading. Home page set isHeaderOnDark: true.
decisions.headerLogoVariants: The source ships TWO logo assets — Directus logo (dark grey wordmark, for the white inner-page bar) and logo_home (white wordmark, for the transparent bar over the blue hero), both 560x56. The port used the dark one everywhere, so the home page shipped a black wordmark and a dark padlock on the blue hero. Both URLs were recovered from the built Gatsby static-query JSON in public/page-data/sq/d/, since no inner page renders locally. The white variant is now public/images/RF-logo-on-dark.png, selected via getLogoPath(domain, onDark) in src/lib/brand.ts. This was a live home-page defect that the header verification missed because it compared geometry (280x28 vs 280x28.08) and never which asset was loaded.
decisions.headerInnerBorderColour: The source header border is -border #dadada (colors.scss wins over borders.scss #ccc — it is imported later and neither is !default). Reused the existing --border-on-light rgb(215 215 215) rather than minting a near-duplicate: 3/255 apart, on a 1px rule that appears only at desktop, with nothing adjacent to compare it against. Accepted divergence.
decisions.headerInnerDropdownHover: The source only opens the desktop dropdown on hover inside the ___home variant — the ul { display: block } rule lives under header__navlist___home and has no base-variant counterpart. Whether inner pages open dropdowns some other way could not be determined, because no inner page renders locally. The port keeps hover-to-open identical in both variants rather than reproducing what may be a source bug. Re-check when an inner page is ported.
decisions.testimonialPanelWash: The customer-quote panel (source section 20) is rgb(242 250 252), a very light CYAN wash derived from the brand cyan. Minted as --surface-brand-cyan-wash rather than reusing --surface-on-light-canvas rgb(245 245 245): every existing on-light surface in this theme is neutral grey, so the closest match is visibly the wrong hue on a 1170x414 panel. Named to sit with --surface-brand-cyan / -light / -hover.
decisions.section19RegisteredOffice: Source section 19 ("Use our impressive address") reuses the EXISTING registeredOfficeAddress block rather than adding a second block for one concept. That block was built for the public-brand design — an address card with an office photo — and was on no page, so it was retargeted: the address textarea became serviceTitle + description, and the component and styles were rewritten to the source layout. Verified EXACT at 1440 (every element same top and size, section 628px) and exact section height at 390 and 768.
decisions.section20CustomerQuote: Source section 20 is a customer quote on a cyan-wash panel with a 323x323 author photo. NEITHER existing testimonial block fits — testimonialBanner and servicesTestimonial are both Trustpilot banners with a widget and a quote-mark glyph, despite their names. A new customerQuote block was authored. Section height matches exactly at 768 and 1440 and is 3px under at 390.
decisions.section20ImageOverflow: ACCEPTED DIVERGENCE: on the source the 323px author photo overflows a SHORTER column (302px at tablet, 350px from 1023) and sits asymmetrically within it — 34px from the panel top at 768 where a centred image would be 22px. The port reproduces the column height, so the panel and every section below it land on the right pixel, but centres the image inside it. The delta is ~12px of internal offset with identical section height.
decisions.section22RegisterCtaPanel: Source section 22 ("Are you ready to register your company today?") had no existing block — callToAction is a bare richText field. A new registerCtaPanel block was authored: heading (line breaks preserved), description, a phone link field, a descriptionSuffix for the trailing full stop, and a CTA link. Verified EXACT at 390, 768 and 1440 — every element on the same top with the same box, section heights 320/243/243. The green CTA reuses the existing --surface-cta-success; no token was minted.
decisions.ctaMarginCollapse: The CTA button gap was first written as mt-6 (24px) under a description carrying mb-2 (8px), expecting 32px. Adjacent siblings COLLAPSE to the larger margin, not the sum, so the rendered gap was 24px. Corrected to mt-8. Same trap as the fourSteps card measurement — worth assuming on every vertical gap between siblings.
decisions.section22RegisterNowIsALink: ACCEPTED DIVERGENCE: the source's "Register Now" in section 22 is a <button> with NO href — the destination is decided in JS at click time. The port renders <a href="/company-formation-packages">, which is where that button resolves to for the default flow, so the CTA is crawlable, middle-clickable and keyboard-reachable rather than JS-only. check-links.mjs reports it as a port-only link; that is expected, not a defect. If the source button ever branches on state (logged-in vs not, package preselected), this becomes wrong and the block needs the branch modelled as CMS fields.
decisions.learnMoreInventedSlug: The registeredOfficeAddress "Learn More" CTA was populated with /london-registered-office — a plausible slug INVENTED from the label rather than read from the source, which links /additional-services/london-registered-office. Fixed in the CMS. Nothing in Step 8 reads an href, which is why check-links.mjs now exists: property tables, pixel diffs, the page comparison and the interaction sweep all passed on a CTA that pointed at a 404.
decisions.packageGridLiveChatSweepExpected: The source's PackageGrid footer renders "live chat" as a <button class="...livechatLink..."> that opens a third-party chat widget. This repo has no chat provider, so contactNote renders the same sentence as plain text and the block's config.ts records that on the field description. verify-interaction.mjs therefore reports "live chat — not on the port" on EVERY run: that output is expected, and it is the only remaining difference in the block. Do not chase it as a regression, and do not fabricate a control to silence it — a thing that looks clickable and does nothing is worse than the plain sentence. This becomes wrong the day a chat provider is added; at that point the emphasis span becomes a real control and the sweep should go clean.
decisions.uspCarouselTabStop: The port renders the UniqueSellingPoints items inside src/components/shared/SnapCarousel, which sets tabIndex={0} and role="group" on the scroll container so keyboard users can scroll it. The source has no carousel at desktop and no such stop, so the interaction sweep reports one extra port control ("Top Rated in the UK Over 750,000 c..."). This is a deliberate accessibility improvement, in the same category as the footer accordion headers being real <button>s where the source uses unreachable <div>s — NOT a defect, and not something to remove so the control counts agree.
decisions.packageGridTooltipsBuilt: SUPERSEDES packageGridTooltips. The source has 22 info-icon <button> tooltip triggers, one per package feature, each revealing a titled explanation. This port originally rendered InfoDisc as a decorative aria-hidden <svg> with no tooltip at all — a whole feature lost to a pixel-identical copy. Fixed by extending the EXISTING src/components/shared/InfoTooltip (added `text` and `icon` props) rather than writing a second tooltip, adding a tooltipTitle field beside the existing tooltip textarea in the block config, and populating all 22 from the source by hovering each trigger. The source's triggers carry NO accessible name; the port's say "More information", so the two cannot be paired by label — that is the port being better, not a difference to reconcile.
decisions.jsonLdCoverage: The source emits six JSON-LD types: Organization, WebSite, WebPage, LocalBusiness, HowTo, FAQPage. The port emits the first five from src/components/StructuredData, each built from real data rather than a hardcoded string — Organization and LocalBusiness from the Footer global's company name, address, VAT number and company number; HowTo from the fourSteps block's steps; WebPage from the page's SEO meta. FAQPage is deliberately absent because the source's FAQ section ("Key questions about forming a company", source section 5) is not ported yet. It must be added when that block lands, and check-seo.mjs will keep failing until it is — do not silence that failure by emitting an FAQPage for questions the page does not render.
decisions.pageTitleBrandSuffix: The source's home <title> is exactly "Company Formation UK & Company Registration". The port appends the brand — "... | Rapid Formations" — from getDomainConfig().siteName, which every page in this repo goes through. Deliberate: dropping the suffix for one page would make the home page the only page in the site without it. check-seo.mjs reports this as a value note rather than a failure, which is the intended outcome — the point is that the difference was seen, not that it was removed.
decisions.openGraphImageStillTemplate: RESOLVED 2026-08-03. Was: the port served the Payload starter's /website-template-OG.webp as og:image and twitter:image, and mergeOpenGraph.ts still carried the starter's 'Payload Website Template' siteName and description as defaults. Fixed by downloading the source's own share image (880x440 PNG), uploading it to Payload media as rf-share.png and setting it as the home page's meta.image, so the rendered og:image is /api/media/file/rf-share.png — proving it comes from the CMS rather than being hardcoded. The remaining defaults in mergeOpenGraph.ts and generateMeta.ts now derive siteName and the fallback image from getDomainConfig(getBrand()) instead of naming the template. Any page whose meta.image is unset falls back to the brand logo, which is a poor OG card — set meta.image per page.
decisions.caseStudyMosaicImageRequired: DECIDED 2026-08-03 — a mosaic tile with no image is made UNREACHABLE (required: true on the item image), not given an empty state. The source settles it: CaseStudyMosaic.tsx dereferences node.image.localFile.childImageSharp.fluid with no guard, and case-study.interface.ts types it `image: DirectusImage` while the sibling is `video_banner?: DirectusImage` — the optional marker is deliberately absent, so Directus enforces the image upstream and the state cannot occur. The transparent gap in this port is an artefact we introduced by modelling it as a nullable upload. Rejected SKIPPING the tile, which was the intuitive answer and is actively harmful: the mosaic is a hand-placed collage (six fixed col-start/row-start slots assigned by ordinal, source uses nth-child), so removing a tile does not reflow — every later tile slides into a slot tuned for a different photo, including the scale-150 crops on slots 3 and 5. Below md the grid IS 1fr flow, so the bug would look different at every breakpoint. Rejected a visible "missing image" placeholder: developer-facing UI on a public marketing page. The gap REMAINS as the non-crashing render fallback — required stops new bad content, the guard stops a 500 on content that predates it.
decisions.caseStudyMosaicCrashIsBuildTimeOnly: The source CRASHES on a null mosaic image and that is safe THERE — Gatsby resolves Directus at build time, so the unguarded dereference fails `gatsby build` and no visitor sees it. This port renders per request, so the identical code is a 500 on a live page instead of a red CI run. Same expression, opposite blast radius, purely because the architecture moved from build-time to request-time. Generalise it: any source pattern that relies on failing loudly at build must be re-examined before porting, because the port has no build-time data fetch to fail in.
decisions.caseStudyMosaicNativeVideoNotVimeo: The mosaic player is a NATIVE <video controls crossOrigin="anonymous" autoPlay> with <source type="video/mp4"> pointing at S3 (sp-rapid.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/videos/case-studies/), with volume set to 0.5 on mount via a ref callback — NOT a Vimeo iframe. The source has a separate src/components/common/vimeo-modal/VimeoModal.tsx used by other sections; customerQuote is the Vimeo one. Two different players, and conflating them gives the mosaic the wrong element, the wrong source type and the wrong audio behaviour. Consequence for a11y: the source modal binds Escape on document keydown, which works for a same-document <video>; only the cross-origin Vimeo iframe swallows the key, so the autofocus fix belongs to the iframe path alone. The source trigger is <div onClick role="presentation"> — no keyboard access and hidden from AT. Deliberately NOT reproduced; the port uses a real button, same category as the footer accordion headers.
decisions.headerLoginPadlockGlyph: The source header's Login padlock is FontAwesome PRO solid fa-lock (data-prefix="fas" data-icon="lock", viewBox 0 0 448 512, single path filled with currentColor), imported in sp-rapid/src/components/directus/navigation/Navigation.tsx from @fortawesome/pro-solid-svg-icons. The port had been rendering lucide-react's Lock — viewBox 0 0 24 24, a rect + path with fill:none and stroke-width:2, i.e. a HOLLOW outline where the source is SOLID. Replaced with an inline local component, src/components/shared/SVG/LockSolid.tsx, carrying the path data from FontAwesome FREE solid lock (@fortawesome/free-solid-svg-icons 6.7.2). No FontAwesome npm dependency was added and no Pro asset was copied. VERIFIED IDENTICAL, not assumed: FA6 Free's lock is the same 448x512 viewBox and the same glyph as the Pro one — rasterised side by side at native 448x512 the two paths differ in 21 of 229,376 pixels (0.009%), all anti-aliasing on curve edges caused by FontAwesome's own coordinate rounding (Pro writes 64.47 and 99.82 where Free writes 64.5 and 99.8). Free also lists the two subpaths in the opposite order and uses relative commands; neither changes the rendered shape under fill-rule:nonzero. At the rendered 15.75x18px that delta is far below one device pixel. Bonus fix: 448/512 = 0.875 is exactly the aspect ratio of navLinkIcon (h-[1em] w-[0.875em]), so the glyph is no longer squeezed the way lucide's 1:1 24x24 viewBox was. LICENCE: FontAwesome Free icons are CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) — ATTRIBUTION IS REQUIRED. This entry is currently the only record of it; the repo has no user-facing credits/attribution surface, so if one is added (footer, /credits, licences page) it must name Font Awesome Free by Fonticons, Inc. Nothing was written into the source file itself because CLAUDE.md forbids comments in this repo's source.
decisions.fontMyriadProStandIn: Encode Sans is a METRIC STAND-IN for Myriad Pro Semi Condensed, which the source uses under an Adobe Typekit licence we do not hold. It is scoped to the ported blocks via the .font-legacy-condensed utility; the rest of the app stays on Inter, so nothing outside the port shifts. The wdth axis is set to 75.6, measured against the source's own rendered strings rather than picked by eye: at 75.6 the mean width ratio across those strings is 1.000 and the worst single-string error is 3.19%. size-adjust was evaluated for the same job and REJECTED — it scales the whole glyph, so matching the width shrinks the height too, which is the wrong axis. This becomes wrong the day we buy the real Myriad Pro licence, at which point the utility and the wdth value both go away rather than being retuned.
decisions.fontVariableAxesAndAdobeKit: No `weight` is set on the next/font declaration for the legacy-condensed face, and that is deliberate: next/font only permits an `axes` list on a FULLY variable font, and this face needs BOTH wght (400/600/700 are all in use) and wdth (pinned at 75.6) to stay variable. Naming a static weight collapses the font and the wdth axis stops being settable, so the width match silently reverts. The Adobe Fonts kit id comes from the SAME BSQ project the Gatsby source uses (GATSBY_ADOBE_FONT_PROJECT_ID). Two consequences worth keeping: Adobe kits are DOMAIN-RESTRICTED, so every deploy domain — production, each Vercel preview domain, localhost — must be added to the kit's allow-list or the font silently 403s and the page renders in the fallback; and an unset id is not a failure, it falls back to Encode Sans, which means a missing env var looks like a slightly-off font rather than an error anyone notices.
decisions.mongoConnectionPoolVercel: src/payload.config.ts pins maxPoolSize: 2 and minPoolSize: 1. Recorded here because the comment that used to carry this had DRIFTED — it claimed maxPoolSize: 10 and that the pool 'drains to 0', neither of which the code has done for some time. That drift is the reason this belongs in a facts file and not beside the code. The rationale: the driver default is 100 connections per instance, and N cold Vercel function instances each opening 100 saturates Atlas M0's 500-connection cap almost immediately, so the pool is capped small and kept warm at 1 rather than left to the default. Idle sockets are reaped after ~5s per https://vercel.com/kb/guide/connection-pooling-with-functions. heartbeatFrequencyMS: 5000 (against the 10000 default) is there so an M0 primary election is detected in ~5s rather than ~10s, which is the difference between one slow request and a visible outage. appName tags the connections so they can be attributed in Atlas's currentOp(). attachDatabasePool is the Mongo equivalent of Vercel's Fluid Compute drain hook — it is what lets the instance close its sockets on shutdown instead of leaving them for the server to time out. Re-derive all of these if the Atlas tier changes: every number above is sized against M0's 500-connection cap.
decisions.additionalServicesWideGutter: AdditionalServices' wide-viewport gutter of 180px is derived, not chosen: (1800 - 80 - 1440) / 2 + 40 = 180. That is the 1800 frame, less its 80px of outer padding, less the 1440 content container, halved, plus the 40px the section adds itself. If either the wide frame width or the container width changes, recompute rather than nudging the 180.
decisions.legalSidenavItemHeight: LegalSidenavClient's 58px per-item height is composed, not measured off a screenshot: py-4 (32) + leading-6 (24) + border-t/b (2) = 58px. Any change to the item padding, line-height or border makes the arithmetic — and anything downstream that assumes 58 — wrong.
decisions.comparePackagesCarouselGaps: The ComparePackages carousel gaps were derived from the Figma card x-positions rather than read off a spacing token: mobile cards sit at 0 / 320 / 640, i.e. a 16px gap; tablet cards sit at 0 / 328 / 656, i.e. 24px. The CTA row below the carousel comes from Figma node 4819:400197. Re-derive from the same node ids if the card widths change — the gaps are a consequence of the card pitch, not an independent value.
decisions.servicesCTASpacingAndTrustPill: ServicesCTA carries three spacing facts that all look arbitrary in isolation. (1) --section-spacing-l was CORRECTED to 56 / 64 / 80 (>=1024) / 96 (>=1800) in PR #265 / CORE-3575; anything measured against the pre-#265 value is stale. (2) max-md:py-4 reproduces Figma's mobile-ONLY inner padding — it is not a leftover, and removing it makes the mobile section 32px shorter than the design. (3) The trust pill is pinned max-md:w-[302px] because that is Figma's hard width in the 360 frame; left as a live inline-flex it grew about 30px, wrapped one word later than the design and ghosted against the overlay in comparison shots. Moving the pill into a gap-5 lock-up with its sibling — rather than spacing it independently — removed a 12px vertical drift that was present at EVERY breakpoint.
decisions.serviceCardsTypographyTokens: ServiceCards maps three Figma type tokens, and one of them deliberately breaks the project's default 'pick a preset and trust the auto-scale' rule. Figma heading-500 is 48/56/800/-1px at EVERY viewport with no responsive shrink, so no responsive Text preset can express it and it is rendered with textStyle="span" plus explicit sizing. heading-300 DOES shrink — 20/28 at 360, 24/32 at 768, 30/36 from 1024 up — and body-300 is a flat 16/24. CORE-3721 subsequently moved the 56px line-height onto the text-5xl token itself, so the token now carries what the block used to state locally.
decisions.heroServicesBannerWideContainer: HeroServicesBanner, corrected under CORE-3538. The wide Figma 'Container' is EXACTLY 1440px with no inner padding — the 180px gutter people read as container padding is the outer frame's padding, so adding it to the container double-counts it. The container gap at wide is 48, not 96. The widget slot offsets differ per tier and are not a single rule: at md the image sits at left=44 inside a 608 column, at lg at left=96 inside 486, and at xl/wide at left=0.
decisions.whatIsPrivateLimitedCompanyLayout: WhatIsPrivateLimitedCompany. Figma narrows the 1280 tier to 994px, and that narrowing is load-bearing: it is what makes the heading wrap to two lines. Widening the tier back to 1280 silently un-wraps the heading and changes the section height. Separately, the source image is a PORTRAIT photo placed in a LANDSCAPE container, so the default centre crop puts the subject's face out of frame at tablet; the crop is shifted down ~25% at tablet to lift the face into the top quarter. Both are consequences of the asset, so re-check them if the photo is ever replaced.
decisions.packagesHeroFourCardVariant: PackagesHero's four-card layout is the PRIVACY PACKAGE variant from CORE-3243 — it is not the generic hero with an extra card added. Anyone reconciling it against a three-card Figma frame is looking at the wrong variant.
decisions.trustPilotBannerWidthThreshold: TrustPilotBanner uses Trustpilot's Horizontal TrustBox, which only expands to the full 'Excellent ***** 4.8 out of 5 based on N reviews' string when its container is at least about 860px wide. Below that the widget collapses itself to a shorter string — so a 'missing' rating line in a narrow column is the widget behaving as designed, not a broken embed. Any layout change that takes the container under ~860px changes the copy the widget renders.
decisions.comparePackagesGreenButtonByIndex: ComparePackagesClient picks the green primary button by POSITION (index 2), not by plan.featured. That is deliberate and was a decision, not an oversight: bad CMS data once set featured on the wrong plan and shipped a green *Privacy* card, which came back as a QA issue. Position is the property the design actually guarantees. This becomes wrong if the block ever renders a variable number of plans or reorders them, at which point the highlight needs a real, validated CMS field rather than either heuristic.
decisions.serviceCardsLegacyCardsFallback: ServiceCards and its config.ts still carry a top-level cards[] array. It is a LEGACY FALLBACK, kept only so that /confirmation-statement and /renewals — whose CMS documents predate CORE-3571 and have not been migrated — do not shift when the new shape merges. FLAGGED FOR REMOVAL once those two pages are migrated; it is not a supported second way to author the block.
decisions.searchCTARenameKeptSlug: SearchCTA's folder and TypeScript interface were renamed in CORE-3270 so the block could be reused on the homepage. The Payload slug is INTENTIONALLY still packagesCTA — renaming it would orphan the block on every page already saved with the old slug. The mismatch between the folder name and the slug is the decision, not a missed rename.
decisions.buttonInsideLinkNotCMSLink: PromoTier3 and RegisterOverseas both wrap Button in Link DIRECTLY rather than going through CMSLink, because CMSLink's Slot chain was dropping Button's base classes and the CTA rendered as an unstyled block-level anchor. This is the same failure the CTA/CMSLink entry in QCF_GOTCHAS.md describes; recorded here so the two blocks' apparent inconsistency with the rest of the codebase reads as deliberate.
decisions.combinedPackageCarouselPairing: CORE-3620, spanning RenderBlocks, FormationPackages, ComparePackages, CombinedPlansCarousel and usePackageCarouselSync. Below lg, a FormationPackages block and a ComparePackages block are PAIRED SERVER-SIDE into one combined card+services carousel. Server-side is the decision: pairing after hydration would render the two blocks separately in the SSR HTML and then visibly reflow, so the pairing happens where RenderBlocks assembles the layout and the first paint is already correct. Only the FIRST block of each type pairs, and because ComparePackages compares exactly 3 plans only the first 3 cards combine — a page with more of either block renders the remainder normally. The two carousels sync by PLAN INDEX, never by scroll pixels: the card widths and gaps differ between them, so a pixel-based sync drifts further apart the more the user scrolls.
decisions.promoTier3CardMinHeights: PromoTier3's Figma card min-heights are LOAD-BEARING and must not be dropped as redundant. Without them the card hugs its content and the pills sit flush against the card edge — that is CORE-3564 QA bug 2. The same ticket's QA bug 1 is the alignment split: tablet bottom-anchors the card content (md:items-end) while desktop centres it, so a single alignment value at both tiers is wrong at one of them.
decisions.sourceBehaviourNotDesignChoice: Three block-level oddities that are SOURCE/PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR reproduced faithfully, not design decisions made here — so do not 'tidy' them toward the design system. (1) Testimonials: production renders the block edge-to-edge below lg with NO outer vertical padding. (2) WiseBusinessAccount: production wraps the block in a surface-tertiary grey-100 surround below md. (3) WhyChooseUs: the source renders a PLAIN card when no URL is set and wraps the WHOLE card in an anchor when one is — i.e. the link is card-level, not a CTA inside the card, and the no-URL case is a real state rather than a fallback.
decisions.authoredLineBreakControl:
Two places where the line break is controlled explicitly rather than left to the browser. RegisterOverseas' heading carries an AUTHORED
that is shown at mobile and desktop but SUPPRESSED at tablet, because Figma sets the heading single-line at tablet only — so the break is breakpoint-conditional, not decorative. BusinessBankAccountsCarousel's copy is two sentences and forces the break at the end-of-sentence full stop, because text-balance left to itself splits mid-sentence. Both become wrong the moment the copy is edited: changing either string means re-checking where it breaks.
decisions.legalSidenavStatusAndSeedOrder: LegalSidenav. Payload's depth-1 relationship population does NOT return _status on the related documents, so its absence cannot be read as 'draft' — the component treats a missing _status as PUBLISHED. Anything that later filters on _status here has to raise the depth or query the documents directly rather than assume the field is there. Separately, hydrateItems seeds the initial ordering from Figma (CORE-3272) as a ONE-TIME BOOTSTRAP; it is not an ongoing source of truth, and once editors reorder the nav the seed must not be re-applied.
decisions.fullPathNestedPageLinks: Pages/populateFullPath plus [...slug]/page.tsx. fullPath is stored as a FLAT INDEXED field rather than being assembled from the nested-docs breadcrumbs at query time, because breadcrumb-based queries false-match ANCESTOR entries — a lookup for a child path also matches the parent's breadcrumb row. The `/${slug}` fallback in the route exists only for pages that have not been re-saved since the nested-docs plugin landed and therefore have no fullPath yet; it is a migration crutch, not the normal path. The stakes: without fullPath, internal CTAs pointing at nested pages resolve to a 404.
decisions.textSanitizeEntityHandling: src/components/shared/Text/sanitize.ts. The `&` regex deliberately LEAVES entity-like sequences intact rather than escaping them, so the browser decodes them natively — that covers roughly 2200 HTML5 named entities without shipping an entity table in the bundle. Anyone 'fixing' the regex to escape every ampersand breaks every entity an editor has typed. The code-point guard alongside it is not defensive padding: String.fromCodePoint throws a RangeError for values outside 0..0x10FFFF, which a malformed numeric entity can produce, and an unguarded call takes the whole render down.
decisions.selectSearchFocusDeferral: The Select search variant defers focusing its input past Radix's own focusSelectedItem effect. That effect is a PASSIVE effect that runs after isPositioned flips, i.e. after the obvious mount-time focus call, so a straightforward focus() on mount is silently stolen back by Radix and the search input ends up unfocused. The deferral is the fix, not a race-condition workaround to be cleaned up — re-verify it against Radix's positioning behaviour on any Radix upgrade.
decisions.usePackageCarouselSyncEndpoints: usePackageCarouselSync. Endpoint snapping is written EXPLICITLY because the last card can never reach the left edge at maximum scroll — the natural index-from-scroll-offset calculation therefore never resolves to the final card, and the last plan can never be selected. The `programmatic` flag, cleared on scrollend, exists because the two carousels each listen to the other: without it, carousel A's programmatic scroll fires B's handler, which scrolls A back, and the pair feedback-loops.
decisions.smallDefensiveGuards: Two small guards whose reason is not obvious from the code. LucideIcon's name regex handles TRAILING DIGITS (Building2) — a naive word-boundary or letters-only pattern silently fails to resolve every numbered icon in the set. lib/firebase.ts CLEARS its init cache on failure: the cache otherwise stores the rejected promise, so a single chunk-load error immediately after a deploy poisons every subsequent caller with the same rejection for the life of the page, turning a transient one-request failure into a permanent one.
decisions.faqs-two-instances-one-block: Home renders FAQInfoPanel twice (index.tsx:78 slug=home-key-questions -> §6, 8 items; index.tsx:127 slug=home -> §23, 9 items). Ported as ONE faqs block used twice, not two block types. populate-block.mjs cannot place both (blockType-keyed rank + findIndex replace), so §23 was inserted by one backed-up PATCH after registerCtaPanel. See QCF_GOTCHAS.
decisions.ourlatestblogs-check-order-false-negativ: check-order reports ourLatestBlogs as "not on the source page". False negative: the heading matches source §24 verbatim but embeds a literal \n ("Helpful guides, advice and\nbusiness tips...") which defeats the substring match. Copy verified correct by hand; no action.
decisions.faqs-story-variance-cannot-tell: check-story-variance reports FAQs as 0 missing / 3 cannot tell. Structural blind spot, not a story gap: title and faqs[].title sit in the checker NOT_CONTENT set (Storybook meta.title collision) and faqs[].description is a Lexical blob it never reads. Story hand-verified against reference/story.md instead. NOT a pass.
decisions.blockSlugs-sourceOrder-authored: .port-source-facts.json blockSlugs was empty, so no spec carried sourceOrder. Derived from list-sections.mjs and written identically into all four specs: landingHero,uniqueSellingPoints,packageGrid,faqs,fourSteps,bCorpCertification,caseStudyMosaic,registerOverseas,registeredOfficeAddress,customerQuote,registerCtaPanel,ourLatestBlogs.

Tiles are a ul/li list rather than the source div soup.

decisions.bankingPartners-tooltip-modal-not-built: SOURCE HAS INTERACTION, PORT SHIPPED STATIC — OPEN DECISION. BankAdsGrid.tsx: above 768px each bank tile is a Tooltip trigger showing per-bank markdown copy; at/below 768px it is a Modal trigger with the same copy. detect-behaviour.mjs exited 0 ("safe to port as static layout") while printing 13 click-target signals. Port has no tooltip, no modal, and no per-bank description field in the schema. Building it later = client component + a11y + a description richText field on the banks array.
decisions.bankingPartners-tile-bg-position: Source randomises each tile background-position with Math.random() in BankAdsGrid.tsx. Port uses a fixed 50% -250px — deliberate, a random value cannot be reproduced or verified.
decisions.bankingPartners-brandcolour-is-content: Per-bank brand colours (#4DAFEA Barclays, #401664 NatWest, ...) are a brandColour CMS field on the banks array, NOT theme tokens. Per the skill: per-item brand colours are content. Nothing added to globals.css or tailwind.config.mjs.
decisions.ctalink-green-vs-cyan: DEFECT, CROSS-CUTTING, NOT FIXED. Source Learn More CTA paints rgb(0 182 122) = --surface-cta-success (green). Shared CtaLink is bound to --surface-brand-cyan = rgb(0 177 227) (blue). Every block using CtaLink renders the wrong colour, including registerOverseas and ourLatestBlogs already live. Belongs to theme-foundation, settle once.
decisions.ourlatestblogs-height-divergence: compare-page @1440 reports ourLatestBlogs 606 (source) -> 1043 (port), +437. NOT a port layout defect: the source renders its blog cards with ZERO images (LazyLoad wrapper measures 375x0 even after scrolling the full page) and cards fixed at 377x375, because the local source cannot fetch the blog API. Related to the known wrong-brand blog API (qualityformationsblog.co.uk). Do NOT tune the port to match a degraded source render; re-compare once the blog API is corrected.
decisions.formationVideo-vimeo-not-mp4: Home §14 modal payload is a Vimeo iframe (https://player.vimeo.com/video/1119340122), NOT an mp4 — the opposite of §13 caseStudyMosaic. Shared VideoModal takes its iframe branch automatically; no fork. showPlayIcon defaults false because the source still has the play triangle baked into the artwork.
decisions.populate-resort-collapses-duplicate-bloc: Populating ANY block on a page re-sorts the whole layout, and two blocks sharing a blockType collapse to one rank — so the two faqs instances were pulled adjacent (positions 4,5) undoing the earlier placement. Repaired with one backed-up PATCH. Any future populate on this page will do it again; re-check order every time.
decisions.ourlatestblogs-line-clamp-dead: OurLatestBlogs.styles.ts carried cardDescription: 'mb-4 line-clamp-3 block …'. line-clamp-3 expands to display:-webkit-box + -webkit-box-orient:vertical + -webkit-line-clamp:3, so the sibling `block` utility overwrote the display and the clamp did nothing. The excerpt rendered 450px / 15 lines instead of 90px / 3 lines, which made each blog card 820px tall against the source's 375 — a 445px per-card error. Nothing caught it locally: it typechecks, lints clean, and every block-scoped check passed; only a page-level height comparison against the source surfaced it. Fixed by deleting `block` (line-clamp already produces a block-level -webkit-box, so it bought nothing). Rule going forward: never put a display utility in the same class list as line-clamp-N, and verify a clamp by asserting getComputedStyle(el).display === '-webkit-box' plus the rendered height, not by confirming the class is present.
decisions.ourlatestblogs-cta-block-prop-is-mobile-: The 'Read Post' CTA was authored as <CtaLink … block>, applying full width at every breakpoint and rendering 327px wide at 1440. The source scopes its btnBlock modifier to a mobile-only media query: the CTA is 300px at 390 but only 117px from 768 up — so the port was 210px too wide on desktop. Fixed by dropping the `block` prop entirely and driving the width from the wrapper instead — 'flex flex-col pt-4 md:flex-row' stretches the child on mobile and lets it hug from md up. Deliberately kept in block code rather than overriding the shared CtaLink from a call site (a md:w-auto className on the CTA would have rendered identically and been the wrong layer, per the repo's no-overriding-base-components rule). The pt-4 also replaced an mt-4 that was collapsing against the description's mb-4.
decisions.payload-template-branding-removed: The repo was seeded from the Payload website template and still shipped the template's brand string. src/plugins/index.ts supplied the SEO plugin's generateTitle fallback, so every page with an empty SEO title rendered '… | Payload Website Template'; three route files hardcoded the same string into <title> directly — src/app/(frontend)/posts/page.tsx, src/app/(frontend)/posts/page/[pageNumber]/page.tsx and src/app/(frontend)/search/page.tsx. Invisible to every screenshot, DOM-diff and geometry check because it lives only in the tab, the SERP and link previews. Fixed by reading siteName from getDomainConfig(getBrand()) in src/lib/brand.ts in all four places, so the suffix follows the active brand instead of being a constant — consistent with the existing pageTitleBrandSuffix decision. A dead test asserting on the template string, tests/e2e/frontend.e2e.spec.ts, was deleted at the same time; its sibling tests/int/api.int.spec.ts had already been removed in port commit 2b4413c and this one was missed. `grep -rn 'Payload Website Template' src/ tests/` must return nothing.
decisions.ctalink-tone-prop-resolves-green-vs-cyan: Correction to the earlier ctalink-green-vs-cyan entry, which recorded the shared CtaLink as 'the wrong colour at every call site'. That blanket claim was FALSE and sampling the source's rendered CTAs disproved it: §11 'Learn More' paints rgb(0 182 122) (green, --surface-cta-success), while §15 'Our Non-Resident Packages' and §24 'Read Post' / 'View our Blog' paint rgb(0 177 227) (cyan, --surface-brand-cyan). Two of the three call sites were already correct, and the proposed global swap to green would have broken both. Resolved by adding a `tone` prop to CtaLink defaulting to today's cyan, with only §11 passing tone="success". Both tokens already existed in the theme, so this was a wrong binding at one call site, not a missing token — nothing was minted. Lesson worth carrying: sample the rendered pixel per call site (getComputedStyle(...).backgroundColor on the source) before acting on any 'this is wrong everywhere' report; a cross-cutting claim needs cross-cutting evidence.
decisions.bankingPartners-heading-tag-divergence: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from the source. The source emits an <h3> inside its bank-tile tooltip trigger <button> — invalid HTML (flow content inside a phrasing-content context) and outline pollution, since a bank name is not a section of the document. The port renders the eight bank names with Text as="span" instead. Proven visually identical at 390/768/1440 with zero computed-style deltas, because s.name opens with `block` so display is set explicitly and does not depend on the tag default. check-headings.mjs classifies the eight names as NOTES rather than failures and carries an explicit warning not to mirror the source's outline — the source home page skips 17 heading levels across 117 headings, so 'match the source' is the wrong instinct for headings specifically. Same reasoning as the repo's Text rule: `as` comes from the document outline, textStyle from the desktop Figma/source size, and the two are expected to disagree.
